Hi Marcus / Naomi,

Thanks again for the intro. We're preparing to onboard a private instance of Redwood inside our VPC (single-tenant pool, customer-managed infra) and need help sizing the GPU pool and defining an initial performance plan. High-level signals: 

- Expected steady-state throughput: 80 qps
- Peak hourly sustained throughput: 140 qps (short bursts up to ~280 qps for 10-15s)
- Model mix: primary: open-llama-13b-quant (serving 80% of traffic), fallback: redwood-7b-quant (20%)
- Typical request length: median ~350 tokens, p95 ~1024 tokens
- Latency SLO: p95 end-to-end generation < 300ms for primary model (we can tolerate higher for fallback)
- KV/prefix cache reuse expected: ~35%-40% on stable flows

Attached: acme_expected_load.csv (hourly qps profile) and acme_vpc_topology.png (our current VPC stub).

Main asks: can you (a) propose a conservative starting GPU pool and autoscaling policy, (b) call out major network considerations (VPC peering / private link, egress constraints), and (c) list any data residency or maintenance windows that would affect placement?

Lena from PartnerInfra is CC'd; she is our infra contractor helping on networking.

Thanks,
Carlos
SRE Lead, Acme Cloud Solutions

Carlos — thanks for the clear brief and the CSV + topology. We'll put together an initial sizing sketch and run a quick sensitivity analysis. To make the first pass productive, can you confirm the following items (short list):

1) Are the p95 token counts for requests that require generation only, or do they include long user-provided context that should be treated as input-only for KV cache sizing?
2) Will the instance be strictly within a single AZ today? Any plans for multi-AZ deployments in the first 6 months?
3) What are your expected QPS tail characteristics (percent of traffic that arrives in <20s windows) beyond the peak-hour number?

Initial assumptions we'll work from: conservative 2x headroom on peak, enable aggressive KV caching (prefix-aware), prefer quantized 8-bit kernels where possible, and aim to keep p95 generation < 300ms via batching + route-based prioritization. We'll draft a recommended pool composition (GPU types / counts), an autoscale policy (scale-up thresholds, cool-down), and a warmup strategy for KV cache.

I attached our templated capacity workbook (redwood_capacity_template.xlsx) — please drop any telemetry samples there. I'll schedule a 45-minute kickoff later this week; Naomi and Karthik will lead the sizing math.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Capacity planning: Acme private GPU pool sizing request (initial sizing sketch)

Quick first-pass sizing notes (sketch):

- Workload assumptions: target steady 80 qps, peak 140 qps, avg tokens 350, p95 tokens 1024; model primary: open-llama-13b-quant (8-bit kernels)
- Effective token/sec per GPU (conservative):
  - H100-80GB: ~1400 tokens/sec (batching + KV hit 40%)
  - L40s: ~700 tokens/sec
  - A100-80GB: ~1200 tokens/sec

Sizing math (steady state, conservative):
- Steady token/sec = 80 qps * 350 tokens = 28,000 tokens/sec => equivalent H100s = 28,000 / 1,400 = 20 H100-equivalents
- Peak token/sec = 140 qps * 1024 tokens = 143,360 tokens/sec => equivalent H100s = 143,360 / 1,400 ≈ 103 H100-equivalents (we do not provision this fully as fixed capacity; autoscaling + prioritized routing + spillover to fallback model planned)

Recommendations:
1) Baseline private pool: 24 x H100-80GB (or cloud-equivalent); this gives headroom for sustained variations and allows room for batch windows without exceeding p95.
2) Autoscale to a hard cap of ~80 x H100-equivalents using scaled L40 nodes as burst nodes (economics permitting) — scale triggers: CPU/GPU utilization > 55% for 60s, queue length > 400 requests, or observed p95 degradation > 20%.
3) Use prefilling + KV cache warm-up during known ramp windows. Maintain a lightweight LRU eviction policy tuned to prefix reuse.
4) Network: require 10 Gbps instances per GPU host for cross-host KV fetches in multi-host configs; peer latency < 1ms within AZ preferred. Account for an extra 20–40ms control-plane RTT via private link when modeling end-to-end p95.
5) Model fallback policy: route >95% of traffic to primary model until p95 > 300ms, then spill simplified smaller quantized variant to preserve availability.

Open items for the next call: expected backlog tolerance (max queue length), approval for mix of H100 vs L40 economics, and whether we can use preemptible/spot for non-critical burst nodes.

Attaching a quick sketch PDF (sizing_sketch.pdf) with diagrams and numeric table.

-Karthik
Principal Inference Engineer — Redwood Inference
